research_question: What is the effect of diclofenac compared with an opioid analgesic on the risk of requiring postoperative rescue analgesia in children undergoing surgery under general anaesthesia?
outcome_description: Requirement for postoperative rescue or supplementary analgesic medication within the first 24 hours after surgery (dichotomous count: events / total randomised)
positive_direction: Fewer children requiring rescue analgesia in the diclofenac group compared to the opioid group (favours diclofenac)
search_queries: diclofenac opioid postoperative rescue analgesia children trial
diclofenac morphine fentanyl pediatric surgery randomized controlled
pediatric postoperative analgesia diclofenac comparison opioid trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trials or comparative clinical studies evaluating paediatric patients (under 18 years) undergoing any surgical procedure under general anaesthesia
Direct comparison between diclofenac (any route or timing) and an active opioid analgesic comparator (any route or timing)
Reporting quantitative data on the proportion or count of children requiring rescue or supplementary analgesia within the first 24 postoperative hours
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, or study protocols)
No direct comparison between diclofenac and an opioid analgesic (e.g., comparisons against placebo, paracetamol, other NSAIDs, or local anaesthetics alone)
Studies conducted in adult populations (aged 18 or older) or non-surgical/non-general anaesthesia settings
No quantitative dichotomous outcome data on postoperative rescue analgesic requirements
moderators_to_extract: Specific opioid comparator (e.g., morphine, fentanyl, pethidine, nalbuphine)
Route and timing of diclofenac administration (e.g., rectal, IV, oral; preoperative vs intraoperative vs postoperative)
Type of surgical procedure (e.g., ENT/tonsillectomy, abdominal/inguinal, orthopaedic)
Duration of the postoperative rescue observation window (e.g., recovery stay, 4 hours, 24 hours)
Mean or median age of the paediatric cohort
effect_size_note: Extract dichotomous count data: number of children receiving rescue or supplementary analgesia (events) and total randomised/analysed per arm, within the longest postoperative window reported up to 24 hours. For multi-arm trials, combine all opioid arms into a single control group. Ignore placebo, paracetamol, local anaesthetic, or other NSAID arms. Convert percentages to counts if necessary. Do not extract pain scores, time to rescue, or total analgesic consumption.
